methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Cemvita, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Moji and Tara Karimi, has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—spanning adjacent stages and the climate & energy sector, including KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $30M raised and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $57M. Peer-median analysis across the three most directly comparable private companies—KoBold, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy—yielded a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. This wide dispersion reflects material differences in commercial maturity and capital intensity across the peer set.

The triangulation yields a low of $48M, a median of $528M, and a high of $1.1B. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects the early-stage profile of Cemvita relative to Series C comparables. Key uncertainties include technology validation pace, path to capital efficiency, and whether peer valuations reflect durable cash generation or market pricing of speculative upside in the climate-tech sector.
